key_inputs: Registered voters 7,331,981 (Kikar HaShabbat, 26 Oct 2026, citing the Central Elections Committee); 2022 turnout baseline 70.6%.

Final published polls 21-23 Oct: Midgam, Kantar, Lazar, Madad and Tatika cluster the five coalition lists at 48-52 seats and Yashar ahead of Likud (19-23 vs 19-21); Direct Polls (Tzuriel Sharon) has Likud 26 and the five lists at 55; Channel 14 Next Data (Filber on air) has Likud 30 and the bloc at 62.

2022 scorecard (theMadad): every major firm underestimated the coalition; Direct Polls was closest (final 62 vs 64) and Midgam's final was 60. Across 2015-2022 the largest lists and Shas beat final polls, and lists polling near four seats often missed 3.25% (Yachad 2015, New Right and Zehut April 2019, Otzma September 2019, Meretz 2022).

Dudi Hasid (Kantar), published 26 Oct via Kan: opposition voters more committed, Haredi willingness about 75% versus about 82% turnout in 2022, Arab willingness about 65% versus about 53%. Stat-Net, cited 21 Oct, projected Arab turnout 63% versus 56% in 2022.

Gantz withdrew 19 Oct but Blue and White stays on the ballot (wasted, inside other). Ahi withdrew 23 Oct, endorsed Likud, and on 25 Oct the committee pulled its slips so those ballots are invalid. Surplus pairs used: Together-Yisrael Beiteinu, Yashar-Democrats, Joint List-Ra'am, Likud-RZP-Zehut, Shas-UTJ.
Polymarket 26 Oct: Yashar about 70% to be the largest list, Likud about 30%; modal Likud seat bucket 20-24; about 20% that either defined bloc reaches 61.

notes: I anchor on Midgam, Kantar, Lazar, Madad and Tatika, who cluster the coalition at 48-52, and I treat Channel 14's new channel-owned Next Data (Likud 30, bloc 62) as a thin right tail rather than half the average; Direct Polls gets partial weight because it was closest on the 2022 coalition, but its habit of assigning undecided voters to their 2022 bloc is stale after a four-year realignment. The point forecast adds a small Shas and Likud lift for the 2015-2022 pattern that large lists and Shas beat final polls and near-threshold lists fail, then gives part of that back because Hasid's 26 October model has softer Haredi turnout and higher Arab turnout. Blue and White is still on the ballot, so its residue sits in other; Ahi's slips were pulled on 25 October, so those ballots are invalid and are excluded from the shares. Seats are Bader-Ofer on the five signed surplus pairs. Social signals moved about one seat: a late personal-vote wave for Bennett lifted Together, and appeals not to waste votes on Winter and Hendel kept both under 3.25% instead of a Zehut-style online overrate.
